sampling: Logged hot-owner samples only; no population loop-query counter is available.

definitions.c2Queries: Eligible scope/view admission lookups after continuation-local masking. Each labelled/unlabelled family now uses one per-observation result. Cache hits included; not global method initial admission calls.
definitions.c2Hits: C2 memo hits in the same method-owner work quantum. Present empty results count as hits. Different view/policy identity, layer/exclusion/mark/full protection masks remain different keys.
definitions.c2Native: C2 native lookup calls for misses, oversize answers, and observations outside an active quantum.
definitions.c2Rows: Sum of native C2 answer-set sizes. Cache-hit returned memberships are NOT counted again.
definitions.c5Plans: C5 plan factory attempts on memo misses. Includes factories that return native-fallback null. Keys include view/exit/policy/whole original/templates. Not all C5 operations, and not run-global distinct originals.
definitions.c5PlanChecks: Actual canStoreInitial predicate evaluations during plan construction, including evaluations in a construction that later exceeds its bound and returns native fallback.
definitions.c5PlanHits: C5 memo hits, INCLUDING cached null/native-fallback markers. Not all hits are a useful prepared intersection.
definitions.c5PlanFallbacks: Plan misses rejected by native eligibility/capability/capacity limits, plus oversize-key gate when reached. A cached null hit causes native fallback again but does not increment this counter.
definitions.emptyDataReplays: Observer saved-native DATA record applications omitted by a proven empty local DATA entry-plan certificate. Root/reverse/MUST/ZERO/Reach/Target-capable cases are excluded. Actual saved replay is unchanged.
definitions.localBoundaryOffers: Conclusion-local guard invocations at actual producer/result/fanout boundaries. One packet may meet several guards. Pure observer guard calls use count=false and are excluded. Not unique locals, facts or stored rows.
definitions.localBoundaryDrops: Guard invocations that reject a dead LocalVar conclusion on that interface/route. Nonlocal bases and original premises are not filtered. Not a byte-saving count.
definitions.localMasks: Retained per-direction boundary target masks exposed to this method actor. Shared per-method metadata can appear under several context-sensitive actors; summing is not a unique-memory census.
definitions.localMaskWords: BitSet capacity words for retained target masks exposed to this actor; not live-bit cardinality or uniquely owned bytes.
definitions.offers: Loop-output restriction offers AFTER dead-local guard and global boundary cap. One offer can contain multiple scalar memberships.
definitions.bypasses: Restriction offers skipped for run1, Reach or non-growing stored summary geometry.
definitions.scalars: Scalar raw loop queries subjected to restriction.
definitions.observations: Complete observer invocations: one raw per scalar plus each tested proper-prefix trial. Expected scalars+trials.
definitions.trials: Proper-prefix cuts tested in ascending positive budget order.
definitions.drops: Scalar queries dropped because the raw complete observation was empty. Separate from localBoundaryDrops.
definitions.cuts: Scalar queries that accept a proper-prefix DEMAND projection.
definitions.rawFallbacks: Scalar queries whose complete observation could not be preserved by any tested proper-prefix projection.

gates.C2: No cache outside work quantum; result size>128 not stored;32entries, clear-before-insert when full. Oversize result still shared within its single observation bundle.
gates.C5: Plan only for run>=3, no static completion/shared carry, non-ZERO DATA original/output, supported view. Templates+candidate row references<=2048,32memo contexts. Native C5 remains for unsupported cells.
gates.emptyReplay: Only non-root identity metadata adapter, same-direction non-MUST native DATA record, nonzero original and known nonzero DATA output base; all relevant exact enclosing-port plans must prove empty.
gates.liveness: Forward definite plain-copy kills; unknown/throwing kills uncertified; backward mentions/no-kill. Feedback/leave/actual-route masks distinct; physical endpoint handlers/synthetic unknown role keep native order.

definitions.sampling: BIDI_LOOP_BLOCK_METHOD is at most24 completed hot owners selected by physical steps; aborted sample is union of top12 physical-steps and top12 candidate-offers. Missing methods/counters are unavailable, not zero.
definitions.ratios: C5 planHits/(planHits+plans) measures memo key reuse and includes null hits. planFallbacks/plans describes failed preparations only; it is not native C5 fallback execution rate. emptyDataReplays/observations is a mean skipped record count, not an eligible-record success fraction.

limitations: No CPU/allocation/JFR reader was run. Actual CPU attribution remains pending all four commands ending.

C2 logical counts change because the selected implementation removes repeated labelled/unlabelled lookups. Native direct lookup counts remain meaningful logged work but do not by themselves attribute time.
C5 plan hits include cached null-plan markers in general; both runs here log zero failed factories.
A guard drop/empty replay skip is an event, not a unique fact or number of bytes saved.
Physical and summary candidate packets are different event categories; observer scalar/trial counts are a separate mechanism.
Counter counts and phase END-minus-START gauges must retain their source meanings; no peak or live gauge is treated as cumulative workload.

classification.priority: See exact embedded interpreter source. C5 uses mark/restrict/prepare/path-index/union/bookkeeping stages; writer binding separates matching/application/field-limit/selection; local publication separates matching/index admission/snapshot-enqueue.
classification.JavaSamples: ExecutionSample events with a Java stack. Percentages exclude native GC/JIT CPU samples captured separately in collapsed summaries.
classification.allocationWeight: ObjectAllocationSample weight; estimated allocation churn, not retained heap or exact allocated bytes.

expanded-empty-data-observer-replay-inve.text:
# Expanded empty-DATA observer replay cell

Status: source-only investigation, not selected or implemented. No analyzer, build, profile reader, runtime edit, or new experiment was run. Runtime source is e558b496acf82de6ff136325d58f3d90ee5b8559. The campaign was still active when this note was written. No performance impact is inferred from source inspection.

The proposed expansion is safe for the pure loop observer under the closed cell below. No counterexample was found inside that cell. The original direction check and the MUST exclusion are stronger than the DATA-only argument requires.

## Exact current call site

`MethodBlockRuntime.skipEmptyDataReplay` is called from `LoopConsumerObservation.observe` before applying one adjacent saved `Record`. It does not skip actual saved local replay. The observer has a separate subsequent loop over saved NormalTarget records. Its mark-request callback is already a no-op, and `LocalRelationApplication` runs no source-hit callback, live source rule, call action suffix, static supply, subscription, or alias expansion.

The current guard requires a non-root parent, later run, non-ZERO complete original, non-Reach input, consistent original/input kind, native same-direction record, non-ZERO record premise, non-MUST premise, non-Reach record conclusion, and consistent native record kinds. It then prepares the enclosing exact scope/exit plan using the same FLOW normalization as summary storage and skips only when `emptyForBase(record.conclusion.base)`.

## Proposed closed cell

Keep the current guard and bounded exact-plan requirements, with these changes only:

1. Determine the output base from the direction: same direction uses `record.conclusion.base`; opposite direction uses `record.premise.base`.
2. Require BOTH original record endpoint bases to be non-ZERO. Keep the parent original non-ZERO and the actual input non-Reach. The native record must still satisfy its validated K6/kind invariants.
3. Remove the direction equality condition and the unconditional MUST-premise exclusion. Unsupported reversed leaf views still have no observable output. No views need be interned or applied to obtain the output base.
4. Ask the exact prepared enclosing scope/exit plan for `emptyForBase(outputBase)`. A missing/unsupported/oversized plan keeps the native observer application, as today.
5. Preserve all other observer families, all separate saved Target lookup, actual saved replay, actual current analysis, admission rules and complete observation equality unchanged.

This is an observer-result elision. It does not remove saved records, input links, C2 admission, actual mark requests, source permissions or published summaries. The same 32-context/2048-reference bounds remain. Root, run-1, run-2, static completion/carry, unsupported views and ZERO/Reach cells retain the native path whenever the existing plan capability is absent.

## Constructive source argument

Let `R=(P,C)` be one validated native NORMAL record. Let `O` be the complete parent original, `F` the actual input, and `E` the saved row's enclosing output port. Let `A` be the exact prepared C5 plan for the summary-normalized O templates at that same enclosing owner/scope/E.

Assume the closed-cell guards and `A.emptyForBase(B)`.

- In direct application, `LocalRelationApplication.applyRecord` uses `nativeRecordLanes` and `ApOps.applySummary`. `Summary.leafKinds` gives every compiled leaf the target base `C.base`. Grafting changes the target field tree, not its base. Therefore each emitted DATA packet has base `B=C.base`.
- A direct MUST record has a definite lane and a possible pending-demotion lane. Both use the same `C`. Pending demotion only changes the layer to DEMAND. It does not change the base, complete O, port, fields, marks or protection.
- In reversed application, `Record.forEachReversedAt` calls `reverseRecordLeaf`. Generic `revEdge` swaps the endpoint bases. The special forward MUST read constructor also builds its result from the original P. Thus every returned `RecordLeafView.result.fact.base` equals `P.base`. `ApOps.applyRecordLeaf` compiles that exact result; each emitted DATA packet has `B=P.base`.
- `EdgeApplication.put` creates Reach only when the compiled target base is ZERO. Both endpoints are non-ZERO here. No direct or reverse result can reach the backward `sink` branch that translates Reach into DemandTarget. Abstract FLOW application builds a non-ZERO-base FlowTree, not Reach. Demotion and selected protection do not create Target.
- The local enclosing adapter is identity because the parent is non-root. Dead-local guarding may only discard results. FLOW summary normalization changes an exact FLOW tail/premise to STAR; it does not change output base. The exact plan used for this test uses the same normalized original templates.
- `emptyForBase(B)` means no planned row with an accepted entry ticket has a DATA exit at B. Exact ordinary C5 can emit a DATA result only from such a row. Consequently every native DATA output at B is rejected, for every tail, layer, exclusion, mark set and protection payload. No DATA member reaches the enclosing signature.
- The saved-record part therefore contributes the empty set. It has no Target effect in this cell. Removing it leaves adjacent admission, repeat admission, labels and saved Target observations unchanged.

This argument is independent of whether the result is NORMAL or DEMAND. It preserves complete O and all scope/port identities. It does not assert that two different nonempty plans can substitute for one another.

## Traced safe examples

Reverse ordinary FLOW record:

```text
Saved forward R: y.f.*/FLOW -> ret.*/FLOW, NORMAL
Backward supplied: ret.g.$/T, NORMAL
Complete parent original: O (non-ZERO concrete original)
Read view: ret.*/FLOW -> y.f.*/FLOW
Applied result: O -> y.f.g.$/T, NORMAL
Enclosing plan at exact saved E: no accepted DATA row whose exit base is y
C5 result: empty
Observer contribution with or without application: empty
```

Reverse MUST record:

```text
Saved forward R: p.[any-taint]/T -> ret.[any-taint]/T, NORMAL
Backward supplied: ret.f.$/T, NORMAL
Read view: ret.*/T -> p.[any]/T, DEMAND
Applied result: O -> p.[any]/T, DEMAND
Enclosing plan at exact saved E: no accepted DATA exit at p
C5 result: empty; no Reach or Target is produced
```

Direct MUST record, matching the already-tested native provisional-lane law:

```text
Saved forward R: p.[any-taint]/T -> ret.$/U, NORMAL
Supplied: p.f.[any-taint]/T, NORMAL
Complete original: p.$/T
Definite-root lane: absent; provisional lane: admitted
Applied result: O -> ret.$/U, DEMAND
Enclosing plan at exact saved E: no accepted DATA exit at ret
C5 result: empty, despite the layer demotion
```

These examples establish source shapes, not frequencies in the measured projects.

## Actual counterexample outside the cell

A ZERO endpoint must stay native. A source record can discharge to Target in reverse:

```text
Saved forward R: ZERO -> ret.$/U, NORMAL
Backward supplied: ret.$/U, NORMAL
Complete original: p.$/U (non-ZERO)
Read view: ret.$/U -> ZERO, NORMAL
Native AP result: Reach.NORMAL
LocalRelationApplication backward sink: p.$/U -> DemandTarget
Enclosing acceptsTarget: true
Enclosing DATA plan: empty (there need be no ordinary DATA exit at all)
```

Skipping this record because an ordinary DATA plan is empty would remove a Target observation and could change loop restriction. This is the concrete reason to keep ZERO endpoints/Reach-capable cells out. The separate saved NormalTarget family must also remain untouched, irrespective of DATA emptiness.

## Future validation required before selecting or implementing

- Differential observer signature controls for direct ordinary, reverse ordinary FLOW, direct MUST definite/provisional lanes, reverse concrete MUST and reverse FLOW MUST views.
- Use exact owner/scope/exit plans and complete ND originals. Repeat with T-to-U cycle protection, annotation-only protection growth and nonempty exclusions. Empty output is still compared as a complete signature.
- Negative controls: reversed ZERO source creates DemandTarget; explicit saved NormalTarget remains; root metadata path, run-2/static completion/carry, unsupported capability and cap overflow all remain native.
- Ensure the actual saved replay/source-permission/mark-request path is invoked exactly as before. Only the pure observer adapter gets this predicate.
- Cancellation checkpoints and diagnostic counters can change in number; document them as work, not semantic equality. Add skip counters separated into direct/non-MUST, direct/MUST, reversed/non-MUST and reversed/MUST if this is later selected, to measure which closed cells occur.
- Validate the source-step argument against native tests before claiming implementation correctness. No such new test or proof has run for this unselected extension.

## Cost evidence still needed

The current campaign counter cannot attribute saved native applications to direct/reversed/MUST categories. A high C5 memo rate does not measure avoided AP replay. CPU/allocation profiles and applicable record/sample distributions must establish whether the expanded backward cell addresses meaningful work. No impact ranking is made here.

# Candidate-directed static survivor pruning

Status: FUTURE DESIGN INVESTIGATION ONLY. This optimization was explicitly excluded from the current selected iteration. No Kotlin, test, analyzer or profile-reader execution accompanies this note. Current runtime: e558b496acf82de6ff136325d58f3d90ee5b8559. Thingsboard reached run-1 and timed out before a completed/accepted forward run; its incomplete static-completion counters cannot establish whether pruning or later binding consumed the time. The current campaign profiles must identify the stage before any measured-impact claim.

## Existing computation

`JoinedStaticSource.freezeWrites` calls one owner-local `KilledStaticWriteStore.freeze` with the union of `all()` from every admitted exit store and its own private B seeds. This occurs after successful engine join and closed execution release. The stores are detached native inventories, not actor callbacks.

For owner/entry scope o, define:

- C: observed raw candidate IDs in `IntLinkedOpenHashSet` insertion order. These refer to `StaticWriteKeyInterner` rows `(original, raw static result)`.
- N: scalar relation leaves exported from all that source's admitted native exit stores, in BOTH NORMAL and DEMAND layers. Ignore invalid domain rows and non-static results exactly as current code does.
- B: that source's private B rows. Ignore invalid endpoints exactly as current code does.
- G(r): the exact current guidance key: `normalizeFlowSummaryPatterns` followed by `StaticGuidanceEdge.of`, including its `guidancePattern` normalization and ordered input/output mark relation.

The implementation materializes `S = {G(r) | r in N or B}` as a `HashSet<StaticGuidanceEdge>`, even when C is empty. Only after that scan does it decode C and return the IDs for which `G(row(id))` is not in S. No other consumer uses S.

`FlowBackedSummaries.all()` yields scalar fallback rows and `diagonal.all()`; decoding that native relation can expand a packed mark/geometry relation before the hash set is built. `RunSummaryStore.borrow(initial)` is available but is an exact raw-premise view, not a normalized-guidance membership query.

## Result that must remain identical

Freeze returns the same owner, same interner, same observed ID array/order, same lost ID array/order and same peak count. Raw candidate rows retain fields, concrete full marks, original identity, layer-independent raw FLOW mark exclusions and all data needed by actual caller binding. The operation does not apply summaries, compose B, grant source permission, request a mark, add a pool writer, or change either DATA layer.

The survivor predicate intentionally ignores layer and protection because the current guidance equality does. This fact does NOT authorize any AP storage or runtime change to layer/protection. The current full set reads both NORMAL and DEMAND survivors; a demand-only probe is wrong.

## Minimum exact inversion

This version requires no new native summary representation or AP query semantics:

```text
if already frozen: return existing result
observed = snapshot C in the same insertion order
if observed is empty:
    freeze the empty arrays and release mutable C
    return without reading any native/private-B survivor

pending = normalized guidance key -> all observed IDs with that key
matched = set of matched normalized candidate keys
for each native survivor in the SAME existing valid N sequence:
    key = G(survivor)
    if key is pending: mark it matched and remove from pending
    if pending is empty: stop; every observed candidate survives
if pending is not empty:
    scan private B with the SAME normalization and valid-domain guards
    remove matching keys; stop if pending is empty
lost = observed IDs in original order whose normalized key is still pending
publish FrozenStaticWrites and release mutable C
```

Equivalently, retain only a boolean/primitive ID match state for normalized candidate keys. Multiple different raw IDs can map to one guidance key. One survivor must mark ALL of those IDs as surviving, as the current set membership does. Do not deduplicate the observed raw ID array or choose a representative raw row.

Proof: for every `id in observed`, the new algorithm sets matched exactly when a member of N union B has normalized key G(row(id)). This is exactly old membership in S. Early stop is valid only once all candidate keys have matched; no later survivor can add a lost candidate. Construct lost by the original observed array, so binding/seed order is unchanged.

Complexity: auxiliary survivor-match storage becomes O(distinct normalized candidates), rather than O(all distinct scalar survivors). C=empty does no survivor enumeration. When all candidates match early, later survivor expansion is unnecessary. If a candidate is lost, the worst case still scans all N and B. This inversion alone does not promise to reduce that worst-case CPU work.

## Candidate-only native membership option

If profiles show expensive native scalar enumeration after the empty-C case is removed, a stronger candidate-directed query can avoid materializing irrelevant leaves. Keep the same public freeze result and raw IDs. Add an internal joined-only exact predicate such as:

```kotlin
// Detached stopped-owner native inventory, all actual exits, both layers.
fun containsCurrentGuidance(candidate: StaticGuidanceEdge): Boolean
```

Its contract is exact equality with `N.any { G(it) == candidate }`, not summary applicability, coverage, reachability or transitive composition. Private B must be queried with the same exact normalized equality, separately or in the predicate's local union. The view is local to the joined source and released after freeze/binding; it retains no actor/runner/closure and does not become a second authoritative store.

A concrete implementation direction is a header-only normalized-original directory over existing scalar group headers and packed diagonal geometry headers. It must not enumerate every packed input/output mark combination. Candidate input mark selects the packed mark mask; candidate target base/path/tail selects the actual leaf; exact full output mark membership and current native presence decide the answer. Cross-mark fallback groups and private B IDs use the same exact key. A source-local bounded/lazy query view may borrow detached native references for this phase, with no such references escaping into final FrozenCompletion.

Required internal adapters must be proven against each backend (`RunSummaryStore` plain groups, `FlowBackedSummaries` scalar fallback + packed diagonal, and private B). The current source has no complete `containsCurrentGuidance` API. It must be designed and tested before replacing the stream oracle. A one-line call to `borrow(candidate.original)` is not a complete implementation.

## Exact normalization traps

1. `G` maps concrete MUST endpoints to ANY and clears their field exclusions. Two different raw initial headers can therefore have one guidance original. FLOW exact pair normalization additionally maps EXACT to STAR. A raw-premise-only lookup can miss a surviving normalized alias.
2. Abstract guidance erases FLOW mark exclusions and abstract STAR field exclusions. Raw mx variants stay distinct for actual binding even if they match one guidance key. Testing raw Pattern equality is too strict; canonicalizing raw candidate rows is wrong.
3. Geometry equality is not `ops.satisfying`, `covers`, or native applicability. A NORMAL FLOW cover can compact/erase a colored native row. Under current `all()` membership, that absent colored row is LOST even though the FLOW row could transfer that mark at a caller. A candidate probe must not synthesize a colored survivor from its FLOW cover.
4. Read both layers. A stored DEMAND relation may be the exact survivor that prevents a raw observed write from being classified lost.
5. Preserve owner MethodKey plus BlockScope. Shared interner IDs are not permission to use another scope's survivors. Within this same source, freeze currently unions every actual exit store; changing that union to one output port is also a semantic change.
6. B records remain in the survivor set even when public root static-to-static summaries are suppressed. B's concrete ordered input/output marks and full context attachment stay intact.
7. Match existence, not multiplicity. Duplicate native paths/layers/raw aliases do not affect the old boolean survivor result. The candidate ID insertion order still determines observed/lost arrays and later binding offers.

```text
Owner o observed C: [idA, idB]
row(idA): p.$/T -> C.f.$/U    (raw candidate, full marks)
row(idB): p.$/T -> C.g.$/U
Native admitted NORMAL leaf: p.$/T -> C.f.$/U
Native admitted DEMAND leaf: p.$/T -> C.g.$/U
Private B: empty
Old S contains both keys => lost=[]
New candidate matching must also return lost=[]; scanning only NORMAL loses idB.
```

```text
Owner o observed C: []
Native summary inventories contain a large packed diagonal relation.
Old: expand all scalar survivors, allocate full S, then test zero candidates.
New: observed=[] => lost=[] immediately; do not expand native inventories.
The later ordinary native summary/catalog export is separate and still runs.
```

```text
Observed raw FLOW IDs A/B differ only in result mx.
G(A) == G(B), because guidance forgets mx.
One native guidance survivor matches that key.
Old: both survive; observed IDs remain [A,B] for later real caller application.
New: both must survive and both raw IDs must remain; do not merge their writer applications.
```

```text
A colored candidate p.[any]/T -> C.f.[any]/T was observed.
Current flow-backed native storage has replaced that colored membership with a FLOW cover.
Old all() exports the FLOW row, not that colored pair; candidate is LOST.
New exact probe must also report LOST; applying the FLOW cover to T is not a survivor query.
```

## Future proof and native acceptance controls

- Compare exact `FrozenStaticWrites` owner/interner/observed/lost/peak arrays and ordering with the current stream oracle across all existing static tests.
- Empty C with a native/private-B reader that fails if evaluated: freeze returns empty and does not touch it. Repeat freeze stays idempotent; observe-after-freeze remains rejected.
- Both-layer and private-B-only survivors, multiple real exit stores, normalized MUST/ANY and EXACT/FLOW aliases, raw FLOW mx variants, T-to-U ordered marks, ZERO/ordinary/static originals, and owner/scope isolation.
- Packed diagonal/supported scalar/fallback paths: ordinary native `all()` is the reference. Include FLOW cover erasure and protected/color-row replacement histories. Never use a broad applicability matcher as the oracle.
- Cancellation/failure cannot publish partial frozen state. Keep source/native/interner lifetime valid until result consumers finish. Shared directories are not cleared by one owner.
- For a candidate-only backend, prove `containsCurrentGuidance(k)` iff `all().validStaticLeaves().any { G(it)==k }` separately for every native backend, then compose with the simple membership proof.
